title: Plato: Justice, Education, and Philosopher King

scenes.text: Can a state become completely peaceful if everyone performs only one assigned duty?
scenes.narration: Imagine living in a city where there is zero crime, zero corruption, and complete peace. The ancient Greek thinker Plato believed he found the secret to this ideal state.

scenes.text: Like a cricket team, harmony comes when each player sticks to their specialized role.
scenes.narration: Think of this as an analogy to a cricket team. If your wicketkeeper insists on bowling fast, the whole team collapses! Plato says justice works the same way: everyone sticks strictly to their natural role.

scenes.heading: Plato's Three Classes
scenes.narration: Plato explains that the state is just the human soul magnified. In his ideal republic, wise rulers govern, brave soldiers protect, and producers provide goods without ever interfering in each other's work.

scenes.heading: Plato's State Education System
steps: Primary training in gymnastics and music
scenes.narration: How do we know who belongs where? Plato creates a state-run education system with strict screening tests. Those who complete fifty years of study finally earn the right to rule.

scenes.heading: Plato's Communism of Guardians
scenes.narration: To prevent greed and family favoritism, Plato bans rulers and soldiers from owning private property or having private families. Only the producers, who hold no political power, may keep their wealth and homes.

scenes.quote: Those states are well governed whose rulers are reluctant to govern rather where they are eager to govern.
scenes.narration: Plato argues that ordinary politicians lust after power and money, ruining Athens. A true philosopher loves only wisdom and accepts the throne reluctantly, purely as a selfless duty to the state.

items: Justice means performing one's natural duty without interference
State education filters citizens into three soul-based classes
Reluctant philosopher kings rule without property or family
scenes.narration: Remember these three big ideas: justice is non-interference, education sorts your true aptitude, and wise, selfless philosophers make the best rulers. Master these, and Plato is a breeze!
